Building plan

Scrapline

Wash up with nothing but a rock. Scavenge the wrecks, build a base, and outlast the island.

This game needs a keyboard and mouse, or a controller. Open the link on a computer to play.

Your browser could not start 3D graphics (WebGL), so the game can't run here. Try a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.

How to play

Gather wood and stone with your rock, craft stone tools, and build a shelter before the first night. Hunt for meat, hide and bone (bone makes knives, arrows and armour), and cook, dry or eat your food before it goes off. Pick a run when you start: escape the island with the old radio, see how long you can last, or just play. Loot the towns and monuments for scrap, parts and the odd rare gun. Food and water keep you alive; up in the snow, and everywhere in winter, you'll need warm clothes or a fire too.

What's new version 2.3
  • Safer page (2.3). The game now checks the 3D engine and the multiplayer library against their known fingerprints before running them, and the page refuses to run any code that isn't part of the game, so a hacked download server or a sneaky player can't slip code in. You can still play with friends on 2.2.
  • Fair play online (2.2). The host now checks what guests do: nobody can take down, lock, open or claim someone else's base without the code, the claim cabinet or the explosives to raid it. Door codes stay with the host, kills only count for real hits, and nobody can post fake server messages or play under someone else's player id. Everyone needs version 2.2 to play together.
  • Fixes and a smoother game (2.1). Food keeps how fresh it is when you sort it, drop it and pick it up, or get it back from your bag after dying. Fish bite at the sky's real dawn and dusk. Less wasted work every frame, so busy islands run smoother. Plus small fixes: a large box keeps its name while you rename it, crops no longer offer to be watered from an empty bottle, and a far-off flare no longer dims the campfires near you.
  • Choose your run. New games ask what you're here to do. Escape the island: find four radio parts, fix the old mast and get to the rescue boat. How long can you last: no respawns, and the island grows harsher every three days. Or free play, as before.
  • Wildlife that acts wild. Deer move in herds and bolt together, boars keep in small groups, wolf packs hunt together (wary by day, bold at night) and bears guard their dens. Rabbits are new small game. Crouch and move slowly to creep closer.
  • Hunting. A wounded animal leaves a blood trail, and deer, boars, wolves and bears leave tracks. Kill with a knife for more meat and hide; a club or a shotgun spoils some. Every kill gives bone. Arrows that miss can often be picked up again.
  • Primitive weapons first. Bone knives, bone clubs, bone armour, bone arrows and fire arrows. Military guns can't be crafted any more: they're rare finds now (the rifle is the Hunting Rifle), and so is the new flare gun, which lights up the night and scatters animals. Guns you already have are still yours.
  • Traps and fishing. Snares catch rabbits while you're away, and fish traps set in shallow water fill up with fish. Fish bite best at dawn, at dusk and in the rain.
  • Food goes off. Raw meat and fish spoil in about a day, cooked food lasts longer, and a chest keeps food twice as long. A drying rack turns raw meat and fish into jerky and dried fish that never spoil. Rotten food makes good fertiliser.
  • Farming. Crops grow much faster when watered (from a water bottle, or by the rain), faster still with fertiliser, and best in summer.
  • Rest and shelter. A night's sleep leaves you Rested. Indoors beside a fire you're Sheltered: you heal twice as fast and get hungry more slowly. The list of conditions now also shows when you're wet and which meal effects are running. And a large wooden box holds 48 slots.
  • Smooth explosions. C4, satchels, grenades and rockets no longer freeze the game for a moment when they go off.
  • Cold only in the snow. You can only freeze where there's snow: up on the peaks, anywhere once winter's snow settles, and while it's snowing. Nights and swims elsewhere won't chill you.
  • Radiation and infection. A badge at the top of the screen shows when you're in a radiation zone, how much you've absorbed and whether your clothes protect you. An infection now lasts five minutes and then clears; antibiotics end it sooner.
  • Regrowth and a tidier crafting screen. Trees and hemp grow back near where you cut them, as saplings that get bigger, but never inside a base. Crafting is now a page of icons with a card for the one you pick. Hunger and thirst no longer shake the screen.
  • Cargo train. Every half hour or so a freight train runs the railway on its own. Stick satchels or C4 to its engine to derail it, then loot the crates that spill beside the line, and crack the locked crate from its armoured car.
  • Boost and drifting. Hold Shift with the gas down to boost any car, buggy or motorbike. Tap the e-brake (Space) at speed to throw a car into a slide, then hold the gas and steer to keep drifting.
  • Climbing. Jump onto rocks, boulders, barrels and logs and stand on top. Steep rock faces stop you, and animals no longer walk through you.
  • Bigger islands. New games get an island almost twice the size, with towns and monuments further apart.
  • A home screen. Everything in one place, and How to play for anyone new.
  • Cooking. Meals at a campfire that keep you warm, heal you, resist radiation, fill you up or speed you along.
  • Exploring. The map fills in as you travel, and finding a town or monument is announced.
  • Combat feel. Hit markers, and red arrows showing where damage came from.
  • Friends. Add people by tag, see who's online, and join or invite them.
  • Settings. Sound captions, automatic resolution and map fog.

Multiplayer

Play with friends anywhere. Everyone needs this game and an internet connection. Everything in a room is shared: buildings, chests, crops, animals, vehicles, time and weather.

Hosting a game: your own world becomes the room while you play, and you have the server tools (K): PvP or PvE, kick and ban. Friends bring their own characters and keep what they carry. Dedicated servers (the list below) run around the clock with a fixed mode, wipe on a schedule, and give you a separate character on each server, so your own world is never touched. Only the server’s owner has their tools.

PvE: nobody can hurt another player or their base

Settings

Low runs on almost anything; Ultra wants a fast graphics card. Change any option below to make your own mix.

Hyper is the most realistic look, pushed to extremes: photo-realistic lighting, the sharpest shadows, extreme grass, full-detail trees and the whole island in view. It is made for a high-end graphics card (RTX 4070 or better) and will stutter on others. If it does, switch to Ultra or lower.

Sharp and Max only look different on high-density (Retina) screens.

The most frames a second the game draws. A limit keeps motion even and your graphics card cooler; Unlimited (all the way right) goes as fast as your screen refreshes.

A jump · B crouch · X use (hold: demolish) · Y inventory · LB/RB hotbar · LT aim · RT attack · left stick click: sprint · right stick click: view · D-pad: up bandage, down eat, left drink, right attachments, car parts or building piece · View: map · Menu: pause. Driving: RT gas, LT brake, A e-brake (drift) or climb, B boost or descend. In menus the left stick moves a cursor: A clicks, X right-clicks, B goes back, the right stick scrolls, LB/RB nudge sliders.
